How does AlertSystem.java manage security alerts?

Long image

A

Answer

Every alert passes through three data structures. A queue holds it on arrival, a priority queue hands out the most severe first, and a BST keeps it for search.

  1. The queue keeps new alerts in arrival order until triagePending() sorts them.1
  2. The priority queue compares severity first and alert id second, so equal alerts leave oldest first.1
  3. The BST stores alerts by id and rebalances itself, so 200,000 alerts need only 18 levels.2
  4. The 22 tests in the same file check normal use, bad input, wrong order of calls, large volumes and threads.3

Applies toAlertSystem.javaone fileJava 11 or newer22 tests passing

1

How does an alert move through the code?

Diagram structure
  • New alert sensor
  • Queue: incoming incoming
  • Priority queue: triage triage
  • Analyst analyst
  • SOC lead lead
  • BST: allAlerts bst
  • sensor → incoming · submit()
  • incoming → triage · triagePending()
  • triage → analyst · assignNext()
  • lead → triage · escalate()
  • analyst → bst · find / resolve
  1. New alert ↗

    submit() checks the input, gives the alert the next id, and adds it to the queue and to the BST.

  2. Queue: incoming ↗

    The alert waits here in arrival order. Analysts cannot take it yet.

  3. Priority queue: triage ↗

    triagePending() empties the queue into the priority queue, most severe at the top.

  4. SOC lead ↗

    escalate() raises severity. A triaged alert is removed and re-added so it moves up.

  5. Analyst ↗

    assignNext() takes the top alert; resolve() closes it with a note.

  6. BST: allAlerts ↗

    Every alert stays here forever, so find() and findInRange() work at any stage.

2

What is each data structure's job?

StructureJava codeJobMain operationsSpeed
QueueLinkedList as QueueHold new alerts in arrival orderadd, pollFastO(1)
Priority queuePriorityQueue with a comparatorGive out the most urgent alert firstadd, poll, peekO(log n)
BSTAlertBST class, keyed by idFind any alert, or a range of idsinsert, search, rangeBalancedO(log n)

No two structures do the same job. The queue does not sort, the priority queue does not search, and the BST does not decide order of work.

3

How does the priority queue decide who goes first?

The comparator returns the higher severity first. When severities are equal, the smaller id wins, and a smaller id means the alert arrived earlier.

Alert idSeverityLeaves in position
1LOW5th
2CRITICALFirst1st
3HIGH3rd
4CRITICAL2nd
5MEDIUM4th

Test 7 in the file checks exactly this order: 2, 4, 3, 5, 1.

4

What states can an alert be in?

Diagram structure
  • QUEUED queued
  • TRIAGED triaged
  • ASSIGNED assigned
  • RESOLVED resolved
  • assigned → resolved · resolve()
  • queued → triaged · triagePending()
  • triaged → assigned · assignNext()

Rules the code enforces

escalate() works only while an alert is QUEUED or TRIAGED, and only to a higher severity. resolve() works only on an ASSIGNED alert and needs a note. Breaking a rule throws an exception and changes nothing.

5

Why does the BST balance itself?

Alert ids always grow: 1, 2, 3 and so on. A plain BST would put each new alert to the right of the last one, so the tree becomes a straight line.

Plain BST height, 200,000 alerts
200,000 levels (one per alert)
Height in this code, 200,000 alerts
18 levels (measured)
Height in this code, 1,000 alerts
10 levels (measured)

After each insert, balance() compares the heights of the two sides. If one side is more than one level taller, a rotation lifts the middle node up.

6

Which bad input does the code reject?

MethodRejected whenException
submit()Source or type is empty, or severity is nullIllegalArgumentException
resolve()Alert is not ASSIGNEDIllegalStateException
resolve()Note is empty, or the id does not existIllegalArgumentException
escalate()New severity is not higher, or the id does not existIllegalArgumentException
escalate()Alert is already ASSIGNED or RESOLVEDIllegalStateException
findInRange()low is greater than highIllegalArgumentException

Methods that read, such as find(), peekNext() and assignNext(), return null instead of throwing when nothing is there. Every method is synchronized, so several threads can share one manager.
